item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission commissioned research on Queensland Police Service employees’ corruption perceptions to inform prevention work and strategic planning.
item.support:
so the CCC can 
monitor the impact of its prevention agenda and 
inform future strategic planning.

item.text: The online survey received 116 completed responses between 28 March and 9 May 2025, covering police officers and staff members.
item.support:
An online survey of QPS employees was conducted between 
28 March and 9 May 2025.

item.text: The CCC reported that confidential information misuse, bullying and harassment, policy non-compliance, and recruitment screening were among the highest perceived workplace risks.
item.support:
Behaviours considered the highest risk include 
mishandling and misuse of confidential information 
(85%), bullying and harassment (83%)

item.text: The CCC reported that 72% intended to report corruption, while 58% expected personal repercussions and only 29% expected meaningful action.
item.support:
Relatively few employees, however, expect 
meaningful action would be taken as a result 
of their reporting of corruption

item.quote:
There is a firm resolve to report corruption 
in the future; however, doubt exists as to 
whether meaningful action would be taken.

There is a preference for lodging complaints with an independent 
organisation.
